Constrained stacking weights by softmax reparameterisation of the constraint

stack_weights_softmax.Rd

An independent route to the same optimum as stack_weights_response, kept as a cross-check rather than as the implementation. The constraint is absorbed into the parameterisation \(w_k = e^{\alpha_k} / \sum_j e^{\alpha_j}\), so an ordinary unconstrained optimiser can be used. With \(\partial w_k/\partial \alpha_j = w_k(\delta_{kj} - w_j)\) the chain rule gives \(\partial \mu_i/\partial \alpha_j = w_j (y_{ij} - \mu_i)\) and hence

Usage

stack_weights_softmax(
  Y,
  z,
  family = c("gaussian", "binomial", "poisson"),
  maxit = 5000L,
  reltol = 1e-12,
  eps = 1e-08
)

Arguments

Y

An n x m matrix of external predictions on the response scale: probabilities for binomial, positive rates for poisson.

z

The target response, length n.

family

One of "gaussian", "binomial", "poisson".

maxit

Maximum iterations for optim.

reltol

Relative convergence tolerance for optim.

eps

Clamp keeping binomial probabilities inside [eps, 1 - eps] and poisson rates above eps, so the loss stays finite at the boundary.

Value

A list with weights, fitted, value, convergence and alpha.

Details

$$\partial Q/\partial \alpha_j = w_j \sum_i (\partial Q/\partial \mu_i)(y_{ij} - \mu_i).$$

Two reasons this is the cross-check and not the implementation. The weights are strictly positive, so a model that should be dropped only approaches zero as \(\alpha \to -\infty\), and the parameterisation is redundant: adding a constant to every \(\alpha\) leaves \(w\) unchanged, leaving a flat direction. The last coordinate is therefore pinned at zero as a reference.
